title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: width-5 wNAF four-limb scalar recurrence, blocked Montgomery normalization

claims.statement: For uniform s in 1..r-1 on BLS12-381 G1, with public powers A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..n at n=2^20, the deterministic four-limb scalar recurrence in proof.md recovers s with probability 1 using at most 2^129 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, sorting, lookup and verification. Each recurrence step recodes its fixed scalar as a width-5 wNAF (at most 64 nonzero digits charged against at most 255 doublings) and lists are normalized to affine coordinates by blocked Montgomery inversion at 12 field multiplications per point plus one inversion per 2^15-point block. The baby index is two 64-bit limbs because the stage-1 width M satisfies 2^117 < M < 2^118. Peak memory is at most 2^127 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^129 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. No heuristic. The bound applies when n divides r-1 (true at the scoring n) and the attack reads A_1 and A_n.

experiments.purpose: On a prime-order multiplicative toy group whose 2-power dividing the order shares a gcd greater than 1 with the cofactor, recover every secret by the two-stage recurrence. Also check the production integers: M is the ceiling square root of (r-1)/2^20, M fits in two limbs and not in one, 7 is a primitive root modulo r, and every scalar a recurrence step multiplies by has at most 64 nonzero digits in its width-5 wNAF. Not a production cost measurement.
